findings: bfloat16 quantization explains a substantial but incomplete part of the exact-cosine versus Q.ANT discrepancy.
Mean Q.ANT residual MAE increases from 0.001908 at k=1 to 0.011982 at k=8, about 6.28x.
The residual remains strongly phase-position dependent after controlling for bfloat16.
At k=8 the mean residual MAE is 0.011982 versus total MAE 0.015967, so a large structured discrepancy remains after the quantization control.

At phase zero the Q.ANT residual stays near 0.00075-0.00077 across k, while nonzero phases can produce much larger residuals; phase representation is therefore an important target for aligned training.
interpretation: Exp014 supports moving from robustness-by-noise to function-aligned training. The next intervention should preserve the locked QFourier architecture and change only the differentiable training response so that it approximates the measured Q.ANT periodic response.
next_research_direction: Fit a fixed differentiable periodic surrogate to Q.ANT CPU-backend response samples, then compare exact-cosine training against surrogate-aligned training on locked QFourier g4 and g8 models.
limitations: CPU backend only; no photonic hardware performance claim.
Synthetic scalar sweep rather than learned activation distributions.
MAE components are not additive because quantization and Q.ANT residual errors can partially cancel.
